result:
The proposed answer of 0 is wrong. The limiting probability should be e^{-λ}.

**Where the solution goes wrong.** It counts codewords, but they come in scalar multiples. Each nonzero codeword of weight n−k generates q−1 codewords of that weight, all with the same support. So the quantity that matters is the number of distinct supports, not the number of codewords.

The expected number of weight-(n−k) codewords is about C(n,k), as the solution found. Dividing by the q−1 scalar multiples gives an expected number of bad supports of about C(n,k)/q → λ. This is finite, not infinite.

**Why the answer is e^{-λ}.** Equivalently, C is MDS exactly when every one of the C(n,k) maximal minors of a generator matrix is nonzero. Each minor vanishes with probability about 1/q, so the expected number of zero minors tends to λ. With k/n → 0 these events are asymptotically independent, so the number of zero minors is asymptotically Poisson(λ). The probability that none vanish is therefore e^{-λ}.

This also gives a sanity check: as λ → 0 the probability tends to 1, as expected.

VERDICT: REJECT
